dockets.what: Exceptional case agreement to energize a new 250 MW, 230 kV Google load in San Jose; draft approves with modifications (refund limits, separate Tier 2 advice letter for network upgrades, cost cap reporting, upfront advance ~$600k/MW).
dockets.status: pending (vote postponed Aug 13 -> Sept 3 -> Oct 8, 2026; outcome not confirmed)

dockets.what: Proposed standards for connecting large transmission-level customers such as data centers; CPUC approved an interim rule for PG&E; final outcome pending.
Proposed tariff for customers over 20 MW: curtailed first in demand surges, 15-year minimum contract with exit penalty, customer pays for upgrades.

dockets.id: Silicon Valley Power data center load growth
dockets.regulator: City of Santa Clara (Silicon Valley Power, municipal utility)
dockets.what: Peak load ~720 MW with 500 MW of new load requested, mostly data centers (55 operating, 3 in pipeline); city says grid limits cap new data centers; expansion projects to finish by 2029. Completed buildings (Digital Realty SJC37, STACK SVY02, ~100 MW) waiting for power.
Small Power Plant Exemption for RB Inyokern Data Center backup generators (99 MW).
Small Power Plant Exemption for Prologis Silver Creek Data Center backup generators (99 MW).
Small Power Plant Exemption for Goodman Energy Park Data Center backup generators (99 MW).
Small Power Plant Exemption for NorthTown Data Center backup generators (97.3 MW).
Small Power Plant Exemption for Microsoft San Jose Data Center 04 (97.8 MW demand).

laws_and_bills.name: SB 57 (Padilla) Electrical corporations: data centers: report
laws_and_bills.what: Adds and repeals Public Utilities Code 913.22: requires a report on data center electricity costs and cost shifts.

laws_and_bills.name: AB 222 (Bauer-Kahan) Data centers: power usage effectiveness: cost shifts
laws_and_bills.what: Would have required data center energy use (PUE) reporting and addressed cost shifts; placed on Senate Appropriations suspense file 2025-08-18 and the 2025-26 session ended.

laws_and_bills.name: AB 93 Water resources: data centers
laws_and_bills.what: Data center water-use disclosure bill; vetoed by Gov. Newsom in 2025 (leginfo status: Vetoed). KQED reports a similar bill reached his desk in 2026 (number not confirmed).

laws_and_bills.name: SB 58 (Padilla, 2025) Sales and use tax: certified data center facilities
laws_and_bills.what: As introduced (2025-01-08) it would have cut the state sales/use tax on qualified data center equipment to a 2% maximum for up to 20 years (not past 2045) for certified data centers with $200M+ investment, 20+ county jobs, 70%+ carbon-free energy, recycled-water cooling and no diesel backup (Ryan LLC summary, https://ryan.com/insights/ca-new-certified-data-center-facility-exemption). The bill was amended in the Assembly in 2026 and chaptered on 2026-09-20 (Chapter 411, Statutes of 2026) as an unrelated hydrogen sulfide air quality standard, so the data center exemption did not become law.

local_rules.what: Emergency moratorium on data center projects on county land (45 days, adopted June 2026), extended through May 2027; county forming advisory committee to report in January.
Emergency moratorium on data centers in city, adopted early June 2026, extended through May 2027.
Council voted 5-0 on July 1, 2026 to develop a permanent data center ban.
Council voted 3-2 on July 14, 2026 to advance a ban within city limits.
Residents gathering signatures for an 'Imperial County Data Center Prohibition Act' for the November 2026 ballot.
Urgency ordinance (5-0) pausing new land-use approvals for large data centers in unincorporated areas for 45 days, extendable; study due within six months.
City Council removed data centers from its 2026-28 economic development plan (Sept 1, 2026) pending listening sessions; no moratorium.
City tightened approvals for data centers (details not read).
Data centers need a special use permit at a public hearing; staff to bring uniform data center standards (labor, environment, ratepayer protection, community benefits) to council by year end.
City says Silicon Valley Power grid limits effectively cap new data centers; it has turned away proposals beyond those SVP already approved.

incentives.name: No data-center-specific state tax break
incentives.what: California has no enacted sales tax or property tax break written for data centers as of 2026-10-15. The one proposal found, SB 58 (2025), was not enacted in that form (see laws_and_bills).

incentives.name: Partial sales and use tax exemption (manufacturing, R&D, power generation)
incentives.what: Partial state sales/use tax exemption on qualifying machinery and equipment for manufacturers, certain R&D firms and (since 2018) electric power generators and distributors; sunset extended to June 30, 2030. The CDTFA page does not list data centers among qualified businesses (whether a data center can qualify was not confirmed).

incentives.name: California Competes Tax Credit (CCTC)
incentives.what: Negotiated state income tax credit run by GO-Biz for businesses of any industry that locate or grow in California; over $180 million available per year across application rounds. No data center award found (awards not searched one by one).
